remarks: RETRY ATTEMPT (2026-11-17): This is a second pass at the same state, specifically to re-test whether the TLS resets / 502s against *.rajasthan.gov.in subdomains from the prior session were a transient, session-level condition. Verdict: NOT improved. All seven *.rajasthan.gov.in subdomains that failed before (rajfab, swcs, labour, rpcb, egazette, bip, invest) plus the bare rajasthan.gov.in host were re-tested multiple times this session (including one verbose run on rajfab showing the TLS ClientHello sent and then an immediate 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' after the CONNECT tunnel itself succeeded) and every single one failed again, identically to before.

A control test confirms this is specific to rajasthan.gov.in and its subdomains, not a general network outage this session: unrelated .gov.in hosts (www.india.gov.in, negd.gov.in, nsws.gov.in) all resolved fine with HTTP 200 and real content, both before and during this retry. This points to rajasthan.gov.in's own edge/WAF or TLS termination actively blocking or resetting connections from this session's egress IP/proxy, rather than a general connectivity problem on this session's side.

Two previously-excluded non-rajasthan.gov.in candidates (labour.gov.in and nsws.gov.in/portal/rajasthan) did change behavior slightly: both returned HTTP 200 consistently this time (they were already 200 last time too, so no change there), but both are still empty client-rendered JS/React application shells with zero server-rendered text, so they remain unverifiable via curl under the spec's rules. No net change in outcome.

Tried two new candidate avenues this retry that were not attempted previously, in case they offered an alternate independent route to the same underlying Rajasthan Factories Rules content: central egazette.gov.in (failed on a local TLS certificate-chain error, not bypassed per the no-disable-verification rule) and data.gov.in (HTTP 503). Neither panned out.

Net result: verifiedSources is unchanged at 3 entries (all re-confirmed as still live and correct this session), and excluded grew from 14 to 16 entries (two new unsuccessful avenues tried and documented, all original 14 re-confirmed as still failing for the same reasons). This retry did not improve on the original — the underlying network condition blocking rajasthan.gov.in and its subdomains persists unchanged across sessions, so RajFAB (the actual Rajasthan Factory License portal) remains verifiable only secondhand via the NIC directory entry, not directly.
